advantages: Removes the trusted central party across organisations, which is the only saving that pays for the overhead.
One shared history removes duplicated reconciliation work.
Any participant can verify the record independently.
limitations: Much slower and dearer than a database for the same write.
Governance has no natural authority — decisions become social.
Recovery from error requires consensus, not an admin action.
Blockchain Evolution.memoryTrick: **Central ledger → copies → hash links → consensus → contracts.** Each step removes one trusted party.

Blockchain Structure.memoryTrick: **Header proves, body carries.** Previous hash + Merkle root live in the header.

Blockchain Characteristics.memoryTrick: **Every property is a mechanism:** immutability←hash links, decentralisation←replication, transparency←public data, integrity←Merkle root.

Blockchain Application Example: Escrow.scenario: A freelance marketplace: the client will not pay first and the freelancer will not deliver first. Both need a neutral holder that releases on a condition code can actually evaluate.
advantages: Custody is programmatic, so neither party can move funds unilaterally mid-deal.
Release and fee deduction happen in one atomic transaction.
The condition and the payout are both auditable afterwards.
limitations: The contract can only check an objective condition — it cannot judge quality.
It depends on an oracle, which becomes the weakest link.
Without a timeout path, funds can be stuck forever.
Blockchain Application Example: Escrow.memoryTrick: **Deposit → held → condition → release OR refund.** The contract is the middleman.

Blockchain Stack.memoryTrick: **App → Contract → Protocol → Data → Ledger.** Read top-down; the user touches only the top.

Blockchain Benefits & Challenges.memoryTrick: **Same property, two sides:** no single owner = no single point of failure AND no single point of control.
